source_refs.note: Exercise 11.1, Question 1: book page 290 (Q1-Q8). The book prints no answers for Unit 11; every answer here is ours.

blocks.prompt: 1. Give two real-life examples where vector-valued functions are necessary.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh theory ka sawal hai: humein do aisi real-life situations batani hain jahan sirf ek number kaafi nahin hota aur vector function zaroori ho jata hai.
Pehchan ka tareeqa yeh hai: jis cheez ke do ya teen coordinates (yani direction bhi) waqt ke saath badal rahe hon, wahan vector-valued function chahiye.
Plan: har situation ke liye pehle axes chunenge, phir \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}\) (aur \(\hat{k}\)) ke saath \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) likhenge, aur aakhir mein samjhayenge ke ek akela number kyun fail hota hai.
Yaad rahe, kitab ke apne examples (projectile aur drone) bhi isi qism ke hain.
steps:
Diya gaya: 11.1.2 ki definition: vector-valued function ek input \(t\) leta hai aur output mein vector deta hai.
Maloom karna: do real-life situations jahan aisa function zaroori ho.
Tareeqa: aisi chalti hui cheezein dhoondein jin ki position ke kai coordinates waqt ke saath badalte hain (bilkul kitab ke projectile aur drone wale examples ki tarah), aur har ek ke liye 11.1.3 ke teen steps se \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) banayein: components, vector form, domain.

Misaal 1: hawa mein mari gayi ball (2D)
Batsman ko origin maan lein, \(x\)-axis horizontal (zameen ke saath) aur \(y\)-axis vertical (oopar ki taraf). Maan lein horizontal speed 20 m/s, oopar ki speed 15 m/s aur \(g = 9.8\) m/s² hai (yeh wahi model hai jo kitab ke projectile example mein hai).
\[x(t) = 20t\]
\[y(t) = 15t - 4.9t^2\]
\[\mathbf{r}(t) = 20t\,\hat{i} + (15t - 4.9t^2)\,\hat{j}\]
Kyun: ball ek hi waqt mein aage bhi ja rahi hai aur oopar neeche bhi ho rahi hai. Is liye har lamhe us ki position batane ke liye do numbers chahiye. \(x\) mein speed constant hai, is liye \(20t\); \(y\) mein gravity (zameen ki kashish) speed kam karti hai, is liye \(-4.9t^2\) wala hissa aata hai. \(t \ge 0\) kyunke \(t\) waqt hai.

Function humein kya batata hai
\[\mathbf{r}(2) = 40\,\hat{i} + (30 - 19.6)\,\hat{j}\]
\[= 40\,\hat{i} + 10.4\,\hat{j}\]
Kyun: 2 second baad ball batsman se 40 m door aur 10.4 m oonchi hai. Agar hum sirf ek number dein, maslan batsman se faasla, to yeh pata nahin chalega ke ball kitni door hai aur kitni oonchi. Ek hi function ne dono baatein ek saath bata deen.
Dhyan dein: \(4.9 \times 2^2 = 4.9 \times 4 = 19.6\); square pehle, phir multiply.

Misaal 2: take-off ke baad aeroplane (3D)
Control tower ko origin maan lein, \(x\) east (mashriq), \(y\) north (shimal), \(z\) oopar. Maan lein zameen ke hisaab se speed 200 m/s east aur 150 m/s north hai, aur jahaz 10 m/s se oopar chadh raha hai.
\[\mathbf{r}(t) = 200t\,\hat{i} + 150t\,\hat{j}\]
\[\quad + 10t\,\hat{k}\]
\[\mathbf{r}(60) = 12000\,\hat{i} + 9000\,\hat{j}\]
\[\quad + 600\,\hat{k}\]
Kyun: ek minute (60 s) baad jahaz 12 km east, 9 km north aur 600 m ki oonchai par hai. Air traffic control ko teeno coordinates ek saath chahiye hote hain taa ke do jahaz takra na jayein. Ek akela number direction nahin batata.

Aur bhi misaalein
Orbit mein satellite ki position (kitab ki Figure 11.2), search mission par drone, GPS par car ka track, weather station par hawa ki velocity, robotic arm par lagne wali force.
Kyun: in sab cheezon ki magnitude (miqdaar) bhi hai aur direction (simt) bhi, aur dono waqt ke saath badalti hain. Jahan direction ho, wahan vector; aur jahan vector waqt ke saath badle, wahan vector-valued function.

Tasdeeq
Dono functions ek input \(t\) lete hain aur aisa vector dete hain jis ke components \(t\) ke scalar functions hain. Yahi 11.1.2 ki definition hai \(\checkmark\).
Kyun: agar output sirf ek number hota to woh scalar function hota; yahan output mein do ya teen components hain, is liye yeh vector-valued functions hain.
Yaad rakhne ki baat: jab bhi kisi cheez ke liye "kahan" aur "kis taraf" dono poochhe jayein, wahan vector-valued function hi kaam aata hai.
blocks.final_answer:
(1) Hawa mein mari gayi ball: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 20t\,\hat{i} + (15t - 4.9t^2)\,\hat{j}\), \(t \ge 0\).
(2) Take-off ke baad oopar chadhta aeroplane: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 200t\,\hat{i} + 150t\,\hat{j} + 10t\,\hat{k}\), \(t \ge 0\).
Dono mein position ke kai components aur direction hai, is liye ek akela number kaafi nahin.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab mein Exercise 11.1 ke jawab chhape hue nahin hain (balke poore Unit 11 ke nahin hain). Is page ka har jawab hamara apna hai: qadam ba qadam hal kiya gaya, computer algebra system (sympy) se alag se check kiya gaya, aur ek solution book se bhi milaya gaya. Aap apna kaam yahan wale hal se mila kar dekh sakte hain. Yeh sawal "open" hai: is ke bahut se sahi jawab ho sakte hain. Hamara jawab ek model jawab hai jo kitab ke teen steps (11.1.3) se banaya gaya hai; agar aap ka function motion ko sahi tarah describe karta hai to woh bhi bilkul sahi hai.
